title: Gate stop test sometimes sees the gate command alive
what: tests/test_gate_stops.py::test_f2_an_interrupted_runner_leaves_no_gate_command failed once in the inert probe run of the stale-texts gate (27 Oct): the gate command was still alive after its runner got SIGINT. The outer run of the same commit passed.
why: A flaky test is a bug (quality-gate rule); it turned the stale-texts gate red on a change that touches none of the gate code, and cost a fix round.
failing_case: Gate of wt/stale-texts, inert probe step: library tests failed on test_f2_an_interrupted_runner_leaves_no_gate_command; fixer saw 3 of 3 passes alone and 0 of 12 under 4 busy loops, so p is below 1/15 and unmeasured.
pass_cases: The race in the gate's SIGINT handling (or in the test's wait) is named with evidence and fixed at the cause.
max(20, ceil(3/p)) clean runs of the test under load after the fix.

fact: Decided by the front inside the principles (owner can reverse): the 27 Oct failure is one observation, p is unmeasured (0 of 40 on the old code under load), so max(20, ceil(3/p)) cannot be computed. The cause (a stop landing while Popen returns) is proven by an injected reproduction: test_f3 fails on the old code every time (p = 1 under injection) and passes on the fix. The final code is proven by 20 clean runs of test_f2 under 4 busy loops.
